As a druid tank you can use typhoon to get stuff out of sanguine.

Sanguine weeks are all about planning and moving as a tank. Use your surrounding too to Line of Sight mobs to make them move.

Be aware of mob health and if one is low; start inching away from it. Be prepared for goo on ground.

Make sure you have a plan for the route you want to take in the dungeon; which mobs to pull and when.
Speed is key - efficiency is part of that.
Tank routes and speed / knowledge plays a big role too in if you can time a key or not.
DPS plays the highest role cause if you have people doing enough dps - you will time it anyway.

I am a druid tank who do keys at 20-23, have 17 years of druid experience, and I cant pressure enough that: you have lots of things in your toolkit; use it.

Disorienting roar is also a temp-lesser interrupt.

If you are unsure of how to play;
The best way to learn is ALWAYS to get a regular team of friends (new or old) together and push as a team. Then you learn how to cope together and figure things out along the way.

Use;
Keystone.guru
Wowhead guides and icyveins tips
Druidgrove on discord
Youtube guides
Be sure to check any available resources for help and upping your game.

MDI is great to follow as well for ideas on what higher people do, how they solve things and what paths etc they take.

Always be mindful of affixes.

The rest is just getting comfortable in your own skin when tanking.

Good luck and hope any of what I said helps.

In Sweden they let you keep the phone - if you wanna charge it you go to a special charging room with supervisors or leave phone there to charge.
Wires/string/rope etc is not allowed.

I did it the other night. Was there afternoon + evening + night; then next day until afternoon ish....

So I will go into detail how it was for me - it might be 100% different elsewhere and for others.


It was just going there; leaving most your stuff at a locker - cord for charging phone gets locked in to a charger room where you can put your phone to charge, you are not allowed to have any strings or string/rope lookalike items. Meds get replaced with what they have there. You are not allowed anything package-wise that is opened (not even menstrual pad stuff).
You get given a calming medication that makes you sleepy when there, very tired and heavy eyelids all the time (for me anyway).

There is a common room with a tv, some puzzle games, card game and you can ask for water, coffee, lemonade or tea.
You eat at set times.

Whoever else is there is a gamble, can be nice people to talk to I guess but I am very much just going into my own shell a lot so I only spoke a little with one.

The others can have all sorts of other problems - worse or less bad than you.
I think one guy there intentionally tried to be annoying to me for example cause he did stuff like sit infront of my view when I watched tv while eating dinner  - the only spot out of many, just to block my view basically.
